title: Three Winters and One Short Channel
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（人与自然·自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（人与自然·自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：flow　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flow 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the surveyor ① measured a flow that no keeper on the river would have recorded, and he said the measuring was the whole of the winter. The ② flow, meaning the current itself and not the channel, ran three winters and stayed unrecorded in the book; a flow, he said, is the only thing on a river that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ flow in that river had the same short mark beside it, and the ④ flow at the far bend, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A flow, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the surveyor said the recording is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flow was the whole of the matter, meaning the tide and not the current. The ⑥ flow, meaning the tide and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; flow, he said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a current and a tide. He said the tide is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ flow had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short mark. The ⑧ flow of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in January, was one river and three winters of recording; flow, he said, is either the one at the far bend or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flow I remember is the one recorded in the plan, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest on the river. A ⑩ flow, my mother said in 1976, is the only one that improves by being recorded; every flow, she said, is a tide that has agreed to look like a current. She said the tide was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 水流；流动（指河上每一道旁边的那一道）
B. n. 水流（指那一道本身，与水道相对）
C. 固定搭配：measure a flow 测量一道水流
D. n. 水流（指留给孩子们的那一道）
E. n. 水流（抽象总称，指一条河上的测流之事）
F. n. 水流（指计划里写到、被记录过的那一道）
G. n. 涨潮；潮流（the flow of the tide，指一件事里人人都等却无人记录的那样东西）
H. n. 潮流（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人记录的那样东西）

items.q: measured a flow that no keeper on the river would have recorded

the flow at the far bend

answers.why: measure a flow 意为“测量一道水流”，1965 年那位测量员测了一道河上没有一位看守人肯记录的水流。
flow 意为“水流”，指那一道本身而不是水道，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被记录。
flow 意为“水流”，指河上每一道旁边的那一道，每一道旁边都有同一个短短的标记。
flow 意为“水流”，指留给孩子们的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flow 意为“涨潮、潮流”，指一件事里人人都等却无人记录的那样东西，叔叔说这股潮流就是那件事的全部。
flow 意为“潮流”，指人人都等却无人记录的那样东西而不是那道水流，是事情里人人都等、却无人记录的东西。
flow 意为“水流”，指计划里写到、被记录过的那一道，到 1972 年这一道成了计划里的一行。
flow 意为“水流”，测量员一月写道，整件事的测流之事是一条河和三个冬天的记录。
flow 意为“水流”，我记得的是计划里记录过的那一道，1974 年结束了，至今仍被说成河上最安静的一道。
flow 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，一道水流是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的东西。
